arms.predicted: Multi-restart SA (3 restarts, shuffled greedy, T=0.01 linear cooling) will score higher than single-run SA, with the improvement consistent across judge evaluations (expected ~87.5 vs ~85.4).
arms.observed: h-main scores: 85.86, 86.61, 85.75 (mean 86.07, std 0.47). h-ablation scores: 85.53, 84.76, 86.09 (mean 85.46, std 0.66). Mean difference +0.61 points. Direction is correct (h-main > h-ablation in mean) but magnitude is far below predicted ~2.1 points. With n=3 per arm, t=1.30, p~0.13 (one-tailed) — not statistically significant. Individual run ranges overlap (h-ablation best 86.09 > h-main worst 85.75).
arms.diagnostic_note: The multi-restart mechanism produces a small positive directional effect (+0.61 on average) but far smaller than the ~2.1 points predicted from design probes. The design probes (87.55 and 85.44) likely reflected favorable test-case sampling in those specific judge invocations. Judge variance is ~0.5-0.7 points per run (not ~0.02 as handoff claimed for deterministic solutions), which means the restart effect is comparable in size to run-to-run judge noise. The restart mechanism works in principle (direction correct) but its practical benefit is marginal for this problem scale.

arms.predicted: Single-run SA (fixed greedy order, one 9.3s SA run) will score ~85.4, consistently lower than h-main by ~2 points.
arms.observed: h-ablation scores: 85.53, 84.76, 86.09 (mean 85.46, std 0.66). Mean matches predicted ~85.4 well. But the gap to h-main (0.61 points) is much smaller than predicted ~2 points, and not statistically significant.
arms.diagnostic_note: The ablation baseline score (~85.5) matches predictions, confirming the single-run SA performance is stable. The predicted ~2-point gap was inflated by judge sampling noise in design probes.

discrepancy_analysis: Both arms show the predicted directional relationship (h-main > h-ablation) but the magnitude is 0.61 points vs predicted 2.1 points, and not statistically significant with n=3. The design probe scores (87.55 vs 85.44) were likely influenced by judge test-case sampling variance, which is ~0.5-0.7 points per run — much larger than the 0.02 previously believed. The multi-restart mechanism provides a weak positive effect that is difficult to distinguish from noise. This partially confirms iter-2's finding (RP-2) that multi-restart provides marginal benefit, while refining the understanding: the benefit exists but is small (~0.6 points, ~0.7%) rather than zero or large (~2 points).
